subject.title: fix(reef): add timeout and bounded JSON reads to relay transport

question: Should Reef relay requests use the proposed fixed 15-second deadline across both initial fetch and JSON response-body reads, accepting that a slowly progressing relay response can now time out?
rationale: This is a user-visible transport and availability contract rather than a mechanical defect: the branch changes an existing unbounded request lifecycle into a fixed fail-closed deadline, and current evidence does not establish an existing Reef-specific timeout policy.

options.title: Adopt the 15-second end-to-end deadline
options.body: Keep the current timeout scope after exact-head proof shows both header and body stalls abort cleanly while normal relay recovery still works.

options.title: Limit the deadline to connection and headers
options.body: Preserve long-running body reads while retaining a bounded initial request, if Reef relays can legitimately stream JSON beyond 15 seconds.

options.title: Choose a different Reef timeout contract
options.body: Set a documented Reef-specific deadline or configurable owner policy if 15 seconds is not appropriate for deployed relays.

recommendation.title: Adopt the 15-second end-to-end deadline
recommendation.body: Keep the current timeout scope after exact-head proof shows both header and body stalls abort cleanly while normal relay recovery still works.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current response-body timeout expansion and are assigned to this PR.
